along_river_slope_ft_per_mile.note: systematic error of HAND-as-stage; not corrected. Its MAGNITUDE is measured against the observed 2017 Harvey extent in data/derived/harvey_validation.json (README, FINDINGS section 11): about +22 ft, uniform — this along-river trend is a property of the thresholds, not the shape of the error

known_defect.summary: threshold_hand_ft is a HAND height referenced to the nearest drainage, not the Richmond gauge stage; the HAND reference changes bed elevation along the corridor, so a systematic along-river error remains.

rejected_route_discharge_rating.reason: source threshold discharges lie mostly above the gauge's observed record
rejected_route_discharge_rating.rating_model: monotone PCHIP through median stage of 40 log-spaced flow bins, peak anchored; power-law tail above the record

rejected_route_discharge_column.reason: the source discharge is not a single-reach gauge discharge

known_defect.closing_it_needs: a HAND re-run from the DEM (DEM not in this repo) or per-reach channel bed elevations in the gauge's own vertical datum; usgs_elev_table.csv has 15 rows for 9 gauge reaches, but those elevations cannot be reconciled with the gauge zero datum. See threshold_correction.py, which tests all five routes and closes each one on a measurement.

method: threshold_hand_ft on the Brazos mainstem levelpath treated as Richmond gauge stage, with crossing segments (within 15 m of an NWM stream line) repaired from non-crossing neighbours within 300 m. Segments below action stage, unrepaired crossings and levee-protected segments are flagged confidence=low. See known_defect for the residual systematic error and the rejected alternatives.
